name: Watts Water Technologies, Inc.
sector: Industrials / Water safety, quality & flow-control components
moat_justification: Code-approved, spec-driven components with proven pricing power — ROIC 18-19% in FY2023-25 and gross margin expanded 41.5% to 49.5% over FY2020-25 — but substitutable category-by-category against Zurn Elkay, Aalberts, Pentair and Xylem, with distributor buyer power and construction cyclicality.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: High-quality water-components compounder, moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% at $356.70 in any scenario (weighted IRR 6.9%, IV@15% $115.83); it clears 15% only at or below ~$116.
moat_for: ROIC 18.0%/19.4%/18.8% in FY2023-25 (roic_proxy) — well above cost of capital through the cycle
Gross margin 41.5% (FY2020) to 49.5% (FY2025); passed through ~$40M of 2025 tariff costs — proven pricing power
Plumbing-code approvals and spec-in position with contractors and distributors raise entry barriers
Large repair-and-replacement installed base smooths construction cyclicality; net-cash balance sheet
moat_against: No network effects or hard switching costs — components are substitutable category by category
Concentrated distributor buyer power and strong rivals (Zurn Elkay, Aalberts, Pentair, Xylem)
Commodity brass/copper inputs, tariff exposure, and construction cyclicality
Data-center demand is project-based and lumpy; serial acquisitions dilute margins near term; European weakness
